claims.text: Retention or loss of toughness in high-entropy alloys is governed by competition between dislocation-mediated plasticity and grain-boundary-mediated fracture.
Alloy composition influences the competition between dislocation-mediated plasticity and grain-boundary-mediated fracture.
Processing history influences the competition between dislocation-mediated plasticity and grain-boundary-mediated fracture.
Operating conditions influence the competition between dislocation-mediated plasticity and grain-boundary-mediated fracture.
Grain boundaries and dislocation networks are the structural mediators of toughness retention or loss.
Increasing the concentration of alloying elements that promote dislocation-mediated plasticity will increase toughness.
Increasing the concentration of elements that promote grain-boundary-mediated fracture will decrease toughness.
The hypothesis is expected to apply to high-entropy alloys containing 5–13 principal elements.
The hypothesis is expected to apply from room temperature to 1000°C.
A lack of correlation between composition, processing history, or operating conditions and toughness would falsify the hypothesis.
Observations contrary to the predicted toughness trends would falsify the hypothesis.
